title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Optics — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State Huygens' principle of wave propagation and use it to explain refraction of a plane wavefront.
questions.solution:
**Huygens' principle:** every point of a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets; the new wavefront is their forward envelope.

When a plane wavefront enters a denser medium obliquely, the wavelets travel slower (v = c/n), so the envelope tilts toward the normal — deriving Snell's law geometrically with no rays assumed.
questions.knowledgeNote: Huygens explains reflection and refraction but not polarisation — that needed the transverse-wave idea.

questions.question: What are the conditions for sustained interference? Derive the fringe width in Young's double-slit experiment.
questions.solution:
**Conditions:** coherent sources (constant phase difference), same frequency/amplitude, narrow slits close together, small screen distance ratio.

Path difference at height y: Δ = yd/D. Bright fringe when Δ = nλ, so positions y = nλD/d and spacing **β = λD/d**.
questions.knowledgeNote: β ∝ λD/d — wider slits crowd fringes together; red light spreads them wider than violet.

questions.question: In a double-slit setup, λ = 600 nm, slit separation 1 mm, screen distance 2 m. Calculate the fringe width.
questions.knowledgeNote: Millimetre-scale fringes from nanometre light — interference magnifies the wavelength into visibility.

questions.question: Distinguish between interference and diffraction.
questions.solution:
**Interference** is the superposition of waves from two separate coherent sources — fringes are equally spaced and equally bright.

**Diffraction** is the bending of a single wavefront round an obstacle/aperture — the central maximum is brightest and twice as wide, with fading secondary maxima.
questions.knowledgeNote: Diffraction modulates interference: the double-slit pattern is interference fringes inside a diffraction envelope.

questions.question: What is polarisation of light? State Brewster's law.
questions.solution:
**Polarisation** confines light's vibrations to a single plane — possible only because light is transverse.

**Brewster's law:** at the polarising angle ip, reflected light is fully polarised with **tan ip = n** (reflected and refracted rays perpendicular). For glass, ip ≈ 57°.
questions.knowledgeNote: Polaroid sunglasses kill horizontally-polarised glare by Brewster's principle — that is why wet roads stop dazzling.

questions.question: Why does the sky appear blue and sunsets red?
questions.solution:
Rayleigh scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴: air molecules scatter short blue light ~16× more than red. Overhead, scattered blue reaches us from all directions — a blue sky.

At sunset light crosses more atmosphere; the blue is scattered away en route, leaving the transmitted reds and oranges.
questions.knowledgeNote: 1/λ⁴ also explains why danger signals are red — least scattered, longest reach through fog.
